http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/.text: The new registration system, built on Joget DX Enterprise, brings farmer and land information together across all 10 districts, giving the Ministry a stronger foundation to serve farmers . MOYENI, Lesotho , Aug. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition (MAFSN) has officially launched the Lesotho Farmers Portal , the country's first national digital platform bringing farmer and land information together in one central registry. The Honourable Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition, led the launch in partnership with Vodacom Lesotho. Field officers across all 10 districts will use the platform to register farmers and their land parcels, and to capture information about households, farming activities, livestock, assets and support services. Aare Laponin, Founder and CEO, FiscalAdmin Prior to the portal, farmer information was held in paper files, spreadsheets and separate district-level records that did not connect to one another. Built by FiscalAdmin Ltd on Joget DX Enterprise platform , the new system replaces that patchwork, giving the Ministry a clearer picture of the country's agricultural community. Field officers use the portal to register farmers against their national identity number, capture household, farming, livestock and asset information, and record land parcels with GPS boundaries. Ministry staff can then search and review that data centrally, giving the government a live, national view of the farming population for the first time. For farmers, formal registration means the Ministry can identify who they are, what they grow or raise, and what support they may need, laying the groundwork for future services such as targeted subsidies and input distribution. For the Ministry, the registry replaces incomplete and scattered records with one verified source of data to guide policy and budget decisions. The wider platform already includes capabilities for programme applications, eligibility evaluation, decision management and entitlement issuance, which can be introduced as the programme progresses beyond this initial registration phase. The Farmers Portal is an important step in strengthening how the ministry understands and supports farmers across Lesotho. Having reliable information in one place will help the Ministry better understand the needs of the farmers, plan agricultural programmes and improve the way services are delivered. Transitioning from development into a national service enables the platform to benefit farmers across all 10 districts. Built for the needs of a public-sector team The Farmers Portal was delivered by FiscalAdmin Ltd using Joget DX Enterprise, with several partners contributing to the programme. MAFSN owns the registry, the data and the process; the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) provided the programme framework and digital-government methodology; GovStack supplied the Registration Building Block specification and reference architecture; the World Food Programme supported the implementation, including the Joget DX Enterprise licence; and Vodacom Lesotho partnered on the launch and on reaching officers in the field. The portal was built with the realities of a small public-sector ICT team in mind. Much of the application is managed through configuration rather than traditional software development, including forms, lists, workflows, user access and reference data. This means Ministry staff can maintain information such as districts, villages, crops, livestock types and document types through the system itself, without needing a developer for every change. "We wanted to build a service that could work at a national scale and still be practical for the people using it every day. The Farmers Portal brings together a number of processes that would otherwise remain separate, while giving the Ministry greater control over its own data. We built this as a live implementation of the GovStack Registration Building Block, so it needed to hold up under real conditions in the field, not just on paper. Joget's enterprise application platform enabled a very small team to turn a working prototype into a national service the Ministry can run and maintain on its own, and that is what made the two-year timeline possible." said Aare Lapõnin, Founder and CEO, FiscalAdmin Ltd, Technical Delivery Partner. The delivery approach also used what FiscalAdmin describes as LLM-assisted spec-driven development. An LLM assistant worked against a written specification rather than the live system directly, with each result pushed through the platform's own API and checked by an automated test suite before release. When something did not work, the fix went back into the specification, not into the system directly. Raveesh Dewan, President and CEO of Joget Inc., said the project shows how technology can help public-sector organisations build practical digital services while keeping them adaptable as their needs evolve. "What makes this project meaningful is the real-world problem it addresses. The Ministry needed a better way to understand its farmers and manage information that can support agricultural services across the country. We are proud that Joget could provide the foundation for that work. The portal also shows how an agentic AI application platform can help a small team build and maintain a national service while leaving room to expand it as new needs emerge." continued Raveesh Dewan, President & CEO, Joget Inc.. As registration reaches full national coverage, the Ministry expects to introduce further services building on the registry, including programme applications and input distribution, extending support to farmers across Lesotho. About Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition (MAFSN) The Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition (MAFSN) was first established in 1935 as the Department of Agriculture. Since its inception, like any other government Ministry and/or department, the Ministry has not been immune to transformations and structural changes that have been occurring. Following a government wide reorganisation and restructuring of Ministries and Departments, the Ministry was renamed Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security in 2003. Today the Ministry is now known as the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition. The Ministry's principal responsibility is to facilitate sustainable production and productivity of agricultural outputs and promotion of food and nutrition security in the country. About FiscalAdmin FiscalAdmin is a software engineering and consulting company established in 2015 in Tallinn, Estonia. We focus on assessment, modernisation and development services and technologies for tax administrations, ministries of finance, the public sector and international organisations. Our Tallinn Office, located in the middle of the Nordic startup scene, is focused on the development of products for the new digital age. We develop new operational models for the public sector to help tackle the complexity of digitalisation through the creation of platforms and ecosystems for public finance, revenue management, marketing, e-commerce and public transport. About Joget Joget offers an open-source, enterprise Agentic AI application platform that converges no-code/low-code development with AI agents to help organizations rapidly build and customize enterprise applications at scale. By combining AI agents with visual app builders, not raw code, Joget makes app generation faster, safer, and more accessible for business users and developers alike. With Generative AI and Agentic AI capabilities, Joget Intelligence enables organizations to automate and enhance processes while maintaining oversight and compliance. Through Vibe Composition , Joget enables AI-assisted application development where AI interprets business intent and assembles applications using governed, pre-validated composable components. Unlike typical AI code generation, Joget's visual-first approach ensures applications remain maintainable and governed within collaborative human workflows. As an Application and Integration Fabric , Joget connects legacy and modern systems seamlessly. Its extensible, open-source core and plugin architecture offer unmatched flexibility, and its White Label solution allows OEMs and digital solution providers to fully rebrand the platform. Trusted by startups, global enterprises, and government agencies, Joget delivers the speed of AI with the control of visual development for scalable, intelligent digital transformation. https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2026/090.text: Updated / Tuesday, 8 Sep 2026 19:34 Getty Buildings in the Palestinian town of Deir Jarir, northeast of Ramallah in the West Bank, overlooked by a new Israeli settlement outpost Fiachra Ó Cionnaith By Fiachra Ó Cionnaith A Government MEP has said the coalition should "take another step" and "ban the advertising of services from illegal Israeli settlements" after Britain announced sanctions on goods from Israeli settlements. Fianna Fáil MEP Barry Andrews made the call and said the EU-Israel Association Agreement should be suspended, as Government and Opposition parties clashed over whether Ireland has led or been overtaken on the situation in light of the development. In a statement before a Renew Group MEPs meeting with French president Emmanuel Macron, Mr Andrews welcomed the decision by Britain and nine other nations - France, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, and Sweden - to join Ireland and Spain in banning goods. MEP Barry Andrews said he commends the Government and wants them to take another step and and ban the advertising of services from illegal Israeli settlements (file image) However, the Fianna Fáil MEP added that in his view it remains unacceptable that services are not included in the Government's Occupied Palestinian Territory (Prohibition of Importation of Goods Bill) 2026, saying this should now take place. "Today's announcement by several countries that they will follow the example of Ireland and Spain in banning goods from illegal Israeli settlements is overdue but very welcome. "Countries like Germany and Italy are now clearly isolated in ignoring international law in the Middle East. "It is also especially bitter that [European Commission] president [Ursula] von der Leyen has shown again an abject failure of leadership. "I commend the Irish Government and would encourage them to take another step now and ban the advertising of services from illegal Israeli settlements, as Spain has done. "However overall, as we know, Europe's real leverage over Israel’s genocidal policies is the EU/Israel Association Agreement. Suspending that agreement must be our focus, before Palestine is wiped entirely from the map," he said. Mr Andrews' comments came as Government and Opposition parties clashed over whether Government has led the measures against Israel due to the development of the legislation in this country, or if it has been overtaken by today's moves. In a statement, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Fine Gael TD Helen McEntee said today's decisions follow "measures already taken by Ireland and Spain". More and more countries are committing to taking action on trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory. I welcome today's announcement by the UK, France and a number of other countries, adding to the measures already taken by Ireland and Spain. pic.twitter.com/Kk741UCgDW — Helen McEntee TD (@HMcEntee) September 8, 2026 She said: "More and more countries are committing to taking action on trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory. "I will continue to push for the EU to prohibit trade with settlements in line with its obligations under international law. We are working closely with our international partners to protect the two-state solution, which is the only realistic path to a peaceful settlement." However, both the Social Democrats and Labour disagreed with this view. Social Democrats senator and foreign affairs spokesperson Patricia Stephenson said "the UK government's announcement it will ban goods and some services" is in contrast to what she said was Government's "watered-down version of the original Occupied Territories Bill". "The UK has previously been weak when it comes to taking Israel to task for its war crimes, so this hardening of their response is welcome. "It is embarrassing, however, that the UK is prepared to go further than the Irish Government by including a ban on some services. "The Occupied Palestinian Territory (Prohibition of Importation of Goods Bill) 2026 was finally passed into law in July thanks to relentless pressure by Opposition politicians and campaigners," she said. "But it was a watered-down version of the original Occupied Territories Bill drafted by [Independent] senator Frances Black almost a decade ago and, unfortunately, only included a ban on goods but not services." Similarly, Labour TD and the party's foreign affairs spokesperson Duncan Smith said the UK Government’s decision to ban trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements "should be a wake-up call for the Irish Government". "Ireland has rightly spoken up about Palestine and international law, but those words must now be matched by the strongest possible action. "Labour has consistently argued that the Occupied Territories Bill must cover both goods and services. Government chose to exclude services despite calls from Labour, other opposition parties, and the recommendation of the Oireachtas Foreign Affairs Committee. "Now the UK is preparing to go further than Ireland ... If another major European economy can move to prohibit trade in goods and some services connected with illegal settlements, there is no credible reason for Ireland to settle for weaker legislation," he said. Meanwhile, in a statement this evening, Oxfam Ireland's chief executive Jim Clarken welcomed today’s developments but said they were "long overdue". Oxfam Ireland's chief executive Jim Clarken said Ireland must revise the Occupied Territories Bill to include a full ban on services (file image) "The UK, France, Canada and other major trading partners of Israel have taken the principled step of putting economic pressure on Israel over its appalling human rights record in Palestine. "The UK will now actually go further than Ireland in its action on trade with Israeli settlements. "While the Irish Government disappointingly left out the trade of services in its Occupied Territories Bill, the UK will forge ahead and ban not only the trade in goods with illegal Israeli settlements, but also the advertising of tourism services, and the financing of settlements. "The way forward for Ireland is clear: we must now revise the Occupied Territories Bill to include a full ban on services, and we must use all of our diplomatic efforts to push for an EU wide trade ban with Israeli settlements," he said. He added: "With Ireland’s remaining months of its EU presidency, we have a unique opportunity to push not only for a ban on trade with the illegal settlements, but for a suspension of Israel’s trading privileges with the EU under the EU-Israel Association Agreement. "The people of Palestine deserve action, they deserve justice. The very least we can do is to try to uphold international law." https://www.irishnews.com/entertainment/.text: Entertainment ‘We’re definitely going to hell’ - the man behind blasphemous Belfast comedy show tells all David Roy speaks to writer/director Stephen G Large about reviving his hit stage comedy Three’s a Shroud Share current article via Email Share current article via Facebook Share current article via Pinterest Share current article via Twitter Share current article via LinkedIn lead-art-block.fullscreen-enter Expand Shaun Blaney, Matthew Forsythe and Matthew McElhinney star in Three's a Shroud By David Roy September 09, 2026 at 6:00am BST “The themes within the show and the basic premise are probably more relevant today than when it was written,” says writer Stephen G Large of reviving his acclaimed 2017 stage comedy about feuding funeral directors, Three’s a Shroud. “You’ve a Catholic undertaker and a Protestant undertaker coming together temporarily to try and get rid of an immigrant undertaker. “We’ve seen [that kind of thing] here over the past couple of years. We’ve seen images in the city centre you never would have thought imaginable: groups of people unfurling Union flags and tricolours, standing side by side against this supposed new common ‘enemy’.” In contrast to such grimly racist reality, Three’s a Shroud satirises such sectarian tensions for rude and crude laughs, as warring Belfast undertakers Gerry McSorely (Matthew Forsythe) and Basil Gray (Shaun Blaney) set aside their differences to mount an increasingly absurd campaign against an enterprising Polish newcomer, Irena Bukowski (Nuala McGowan), who’s spotted a gap in the market for a funeral director prepared to bury the dead regardless of their religious affiliations. Glen Hansard’s final musical project to receive world premiere at Belfast’s Lyric Theatre Presley Gerber’s ex-girlfriend says she is ‘very’ angry about his death DLA man Stephen Large's new play takes a look at the funny side of death Opens in new window Review: Belfast-set stage comedy Three's A Shroud puts the fun in funeral Opens in new window Stephen G Large on the return of the Dundonald Liberation Army Opens in new window Matthew McElhinney as Simon in Three's a Shroud Gerry’s enterprising, social media-savvy apprentice/aspiring rapper, Simon (Matthew McElhinney), is also in the thick of this farcical mix from the team behind the hit series of Dundonald Liberation Army (DLA) shows, which is currently in final rehearsals prior to returning to the stage for a one-off revival at The Waterfront Hall on Saturday night. “Previously, I would write the script, maybe pop my head in through the door during rehearsals, and then turn up at the venue in my finest to have a couple of drinks and laugh along with the audience,” explains the Dundonald-born writer and comedian of directing the newly revised and updated production for the main auditorium at The Waterfront - a sizeable upgrade on the original Martin Lynch-directed version which played at the venue’s smaller Studio space in 2017 and 2018. “It’s only the last maybe three or four years that I’ve become more involved in the production side of things, and there’s just so much that goes into putting one of these shows on in a venue of that size. “It’s just a massive, massive production, and yeah, it’s stressful. There’s a lot of things going on.” Stephen G Large in rehearsals for Three's a Shroud However, it seems that Large has loved getting more involved with the cast while directing them as they bring his script to life in rehearsals. “This isn’t a criticism of anyone that’s directed one of my shows, but as the writer sometimes you see them and go, ‘That’s not quite what I would have done’, or ‘That’s not what I meant there’,” explains the writer turned director, who is also a stand-up comedian and the host of The DLA Podcast. “So I wanted to give [directing] a go myself. But, you know, I’m not walking about in there flapping a chiffon scarf or anything. I’m as green as cabbage, so I’m learning on my feet. The cast and crew of Three's a Shroud are preparing to bring the show to The Waterfront Hall “I’m probably the least experienced person in the room, but in saying that, I know how to write a joke, I know how to make people laugh, and I can I can communicate pretty well with the cast. “I’ve worked with all [of the actors] on repeated occasions. They’re great comedic actors, they’ve got great timing, and they embrace the chaos as well. “My shows are just 100 miles per hour, with lots of quick changes and props and just madness, so they know what they’re getting themselves in for at this point. “I’m delighted to have them all on board again, and we have a relationship where if they turn around and go, ‘would this work?’, or ‘would it not be better saying this?’, I’m all ears. “You can’t be precious. Whatever makes it the best possible version, you have to be open to it.” With a chuckle, Large adds: “But the end of the day, I still get a veto, which is nice.” View this post on Instagram To see those jokes land in front of 350 people was amazing. But I always wondered what would it be like to have them land in front of 2,000 people — Stephen G Large Three’s a Shroud was Large’s second ever play, following his festive-themed 2016 debut, Carol’s Christmas, and while the undertakers-centric comedy was well-received during its original runs, he always felt it the show had more life left in it. Thus, when the folks at The Waterfront Hall suggested a Three’s a Shroud revival, Large was keen to revamp the show for the venue’s larger main stage. “It was such fun to do, and I always wanted to give it an opportunity on a bigger platform to see a bigger audience’s reaction,” he explains. “To see those jokes land in front of 350 people was amazing. But what would it be like to have them land in front of 2,000 people? “I had sort of gone off on a tangent with the DLA stuff and stand-up and whatever else, but this show was always on the back burner.” Shaun Blaney and BJ Hogg in Three's A Shroud, written by Stephen Large and directed by Martin Lynch, at the Waterfront Studio, Belfast The original cast have all returned, minus the late BJ Hogg as Gerry. Best known as Big Mervyn in Give My Head Peace, the Lisburn-born actor passed away in 2020. Thus, DLA star Matthew Forsythe has stepped into the role in the new and improved 2026 version of Three’s a Shroud, which Large has brought almost a full decade of additional writing experience to bear on. “There was a massive rewrite,” explains the writer and director, who will bring a brand new DLA-related Christmas show, No Room At The Flat, to The MAC in December. “I’d invented things that were supposed to be ‘wacky’ and would never happen - like live-streamed funerals - that then did actually happen. “So we’ve tightened it and added in a lot more new stuff which is on a par with the best stuff that worked the last time. Matthew Forsythe has joined the cast of Three's a Shroud for its 2026 revival “I’m not going to lie and say, ‘oh, it’s a completely new show’. But with all of the changes and updates and breathing new life into it with the cast, it’s going to be a better show and a completely different experience.” Large still has fond memories of working on the original production with BJ Hogg, whom he describes as “a bit of an elder statesman father figure to all us young hallions”. “BJ was an absolute gent,“ he recalls. “Me and the cast were all in our 20s, and he gave us a lot of good advice. He also told me it was one of the very few scripts which gave him a genuine belly laugh while reading it. “He said ‘I’m going to sing your praises to big Tim McGarry’ - and he did. BJ Hogg and Matthew McElhinney come to blows in Three's A Shroud by Stephen Large “I got speaking to Tim from that, and then I got to work on his radio show, A Perforated Ulster. Ten series later, I’m still working on it - and that’s all down to BJ.” Large adds: “Obviously, when we decided this was coming back, there was a huge void to fill - but Matthew Forsythe was the first and only person I approached about doing it.” View this post on Instagram Despite some of the show’s slightly blasphemous content, initial rehearsals took place at St Mary Magdalene’s Parish Church on Donegall Pass - an irony that’s not lost on the writer turned director. “I’m surprised we all didn’t spontaneously burst into flames,” laughs Large. “If we were unsure whether we were going to hell before these rehearsals, we’ve definitely fast-tracked our entry.” Three’s a Shroud, Saturday September 12, The Waterfront Hall, Belfast. Tickets via waterfront.co.uk .
